In practice, “average” can refer either to the arithmetic mean or the median; real‑estate industry reports almost always publish the median because it’s less skewed by extreme outliers (e.g., luxury properties).

For most practical purposes—whether you’re budgeting for a purchase, estimating market trends, or building a predictive model—the current benchmark for a typical Californian single‑family home sits between **$710 – $740 thousand**.
